---
title: "Chi Square Independence Test for Contingency Tables"
author: "Anthony Morciglio"
date: "10/17/2025"
output: html_document
---

## Description of the Simulation Procedure

The simulation of contingency tables in this example is based on the **Chi-Square Test for Independence**, which examines whether two categorical variables are related — in this case, **Ethnicity** and **Preference (Like/Dislike)** for a collared shirt.

To accurately simulate real-world data, the following steps are performed:

1. **Define Parameters**  
   We begin by specifying:
   - The total sample size, `N`.  
   - The set of ethnic groups, `ethnicities`.  
   - The population proportions for each ethnicity, `pi`.  
   - The probability of “liking” the product, `p_like`.  

   These parameters represent a realistic marketing survey scenario. For example, `pi` defines how likely each ethnic group is to appear in the sample, while `p_like` defines the common probability that any participant likes the product.

2. **Simulate the Row Totals (Multinomial Sampling)**  
   We draw the number of respondents per ethnicity using the `rmultinom()` function:

```{r setup, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, echo = TRUE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE)
library(ggplot2); library(dplyr); library(tidyr)

# Parameters - change these to reflect your scenario

N <- 1000
ethnicities <- c("White", "Black", "Hispanic", "Asian", "Other")
pi <- c(0.35, 0.25, 0.20, 0.15, 0.05)   # population proportions (sum = 1)
p_like <- 0.55                         # homogeneous probability of 'Like'
set.seed(2025)

# 1) allocate row totals via multinomial

n_row <- as.numeric(rmultinom(1, size = N, prob = pi))   # vector length 5

# 2) for each row, draw likes ~ Binomial(n_i, p_like)

likes <- rbinom(length(n_row), size = n_row, prob = p_like)
dislikes <- n_row - likes

# Build table (data.frame)

ct <- data.frame(
Ethnicity = ethnicities,
n = n_row,
Like = likes,
Dislike = dislikes,
stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

ct_long <- ct %>% select(Ethnicity, Like, Dislike) %>%
pivot_longer(cols = c("Like","Dislike"), names_to = "Preference", values_to = "Count")

print(ct)

# convert to matrix with rows = ethnicities, cols = Like/Dislike

obs_matrix <- as.matrix(ct[, c("Like","Dislike")])
rownames(obs_matrix) <- ct$Ethnicity

test <- chisq.test(obs_matrix, correct = FALSE)  # no Yates correction for simplicity
test$statistic
test$p.value
test$expected   # expected counts under independence

exp_df <- as.data.frame(test$expected) %>%
mutate(Ethnicity = rownames(.)) %>%
pivot_longer(cols = c("Like","Dislike"), names_to = "Preference", values_to = "Expected")

obs_df <- ct_long

merged <- left_join(obs_df, exp_df, by = c("Ethnicity","Preference"))

# Custom color mapping for ethnicities: Red, Orange, Green, Yellow, Blue
color_order <- c("red", "orange", "green", "yellow", "blue")

ggplot(merged, aes(x = Preference, y = Count, fill = Ethnicity)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge", alpha = 0.85, color = "black") +
  geom_point(aes(y = Expected), position = position_dodge(width = 0.9),
             color = "black", size = 3, shape = 21, fill = "white") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = color_order) +
  labs(
    title = "Observed vs Expected Counts by Ethnicity (one simulated table)",
    subtitle = "Bars = observed, Points = expected under homogeneity",
    y = "Count"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)

# Simple mosaic using ggplot by showing proportion rectangles

prop_df <- merged %>%
group_by(Ethnicity) %>%
mutate(RowTotal = sum(Count)) %>%
ungroup() %>%
mutate(Prop = Count / sum(Count))

ggplot(prop_df, aes(x = Ethnicity, y = Count, fill = Preference)) +
geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "fill") +
labs(title = "Stacked proportion by Ethnicity (Like vs Dislike)",
y = "Proportion") +
theme_minimal(base_size = 13)

R <- 5000   # number of repetitions
chisq_stats <- numeric(R)
pvals <- numeric(R)

for (r in seq_len(R)) {
n_row_r <- as.numeric(rmultinom(1, size = N, prob = pi))
likes_r <- rbinom(length(n_row_r), size = n_row_r, prob = p_like)
mat_r <- cbind(likes_r, n_row_r - likes_r)
res <- suppressWarnings(chisq.test(mat_r, correct = FALSE))
chisq_stats[r] <- as.numeric(res$statistic)
pvals[r] <- res$p.value
}

# Empirical distribution and Type I error at alpha = 0.05

alpha <- 0.05
emp_type1 <- mean(pvals < alpha)

# Plot histogram of chisq stats and overlay theoretical chi-square density

df_mc <- data.frame(stat = chisq_stats)
ggplot(df_mc, aes(x = stat)) +
geom_histogram(aes(y = ..density..), bins = 40, fill = "blue", color = "white") +
stat_function(fun = dchisq, args = list(df = length(ethnicities) - 1), color = "red", size = 1) +
labs(title = "Monte Carlo null distribution of Chi-square statistic (R simulations)",
subtitle = paste0("Empirical Type I error (alpha = ", alpha, "): ", round(emp_type1, 3)),
x = expression(chi^2), y = "Density") +
theme_minimal(base_size = 13)

```
